instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Impossible Currency
cards.instruction: Price every favor in symbolic acts, imaginary resources, or promises that cannot be measured normally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I put my hand on the wall like you. Payment arranged. You can borrow my ladder for your shadow until Friday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking the plaster. I need my shadow at work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Plaster first. Keep its office hours; I'll take its evenings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you hold the ladder too? I'm afraid of heights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For that, leave me your fear of falling. I'll keep it until you're down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I set a spoon beside yours. Yesterday's measure. I'll fix the kettle for a spoonful of yesterday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's for tea. How do I give you yesterday?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tea first, yes. Start with the five minutes you wasted this morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then leave it overnight. I can wait for the currency to mature.

cards.title: Yes, Under My Physics
cards.instruction: Agree completely, then redefine each term using rules that make your preferred outcome inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I turned my feet like yours. Forward for the portrait, absolutely. Facing you counts; I'm staying in this shade.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bracing the tripod. I need you two feet closer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Braced, yes. Feet are units of zoom. Increase yours by two.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now only your face fits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A full portrait means all the important parts. You've captured me completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've sat backwards like you. Lifting position, absolutely. I'll help move your boxes; help means saving effort, so I'll call the lift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was reaching the socket. The lift's broken. Carry that box yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Socket reached, yes. Yourself means without involving you. I'll hire a mover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll carry them if you hold the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. Holding means preventing movement. I'll wedge it open and stay in this chair.

cards.title: The Logic Gets Bigger
cards.instruction: Use every new detail to expand the impossible system, its history, and the consequences of breaking it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've raised both arms like you. Landing clearance. Our meeting chairs float at noon; they've had air rights since the first furniture strike.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was stretching. Can't we stand and tie the chairs down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Limber first. Restraint broke the last treaty; that's when the desks joined them. We'll need an airspace permit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker only issues floor permits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then promote her to altitude minister before the cabinets claim the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've tapped my bowl with a spoon too. Formal greetings. Yours said hello; crockery hasn't spoken since the Great Washing-Up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was testing it for cracks. It says it wants bread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Vessels checked. Trade has reopened. Offer a roll, but keep the butter separate; mixed gifts caused the gravy embargo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's asking for a seat at dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give it a stool, not a place setting. Plates were how the saucers won territory.

cards.title: Co-Sign This
cards.instruction: Get someone to help by making them an official participant who shares responsibility for the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed where you made that mark. Joint borrowers. Will you co-sign for this barbecue?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was an ink test. I'll help carry it, but the handle looks cracked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pen's working. Sign as joint custodian; we'll inspect it together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner wants a replacement by Sunday if it breaks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're co-chair of replacements. I'll call the shops; you approve what we buy before we promise her anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drew a line beside yours. Route agreed. I've made you co-organizer of Saturday's school trip; will you sign it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was crossing out a closed road. Your route misses the museum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Closure marked. Correct the route and initial it; then we both own the plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fix it, but you explain any delays to the parents.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together. I'll introduce you as our transport lead and take the questions beside you.

cards.title: Close It Properly
cards.instruction: Keep them present until both of you complete the ritual that formally ends this role, meeting, or relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've closed my book too. Final chapter. Before you leave, we say the book-club closing words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was clearing space for my coat. My taxi's coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coats first. I'll say 'chapter closed'; you answer 'until next time.' Then we can leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's here. I'll say my bit from the car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll come to your window. Give me ten seconds of your taxi time; I only need you through 'until next time.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I tapped the counter like you. Farewell signal. Before you hand in your keys, we ring the shop bell together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking which board was loose. I'm leaving because that bell rings constantly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Counter checked. This is the last one you have to answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Ring it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your hand beside mine. One press, then put your keys down.
